roles.purpose: Initialize the private machine profile, generate project-local skills, validate structures, and provide packaging tools.
Discuss state with the user, create itemized proposals, and commit only accepted project-state changes.
Execute one confirmed task and produce a handoff without editing authoritative management state.

storage_invariants.rule: Accepted state/, records/, and sources/ are authoritative; views/ and index/ are rebuildable derivatives and must not be edited as project authority.
Exploration and unconfirmed findings remain under work/ until itemized proposal and user acceptance commit them to records/.
packages/ transports proposals, artifacts, and receipts; package presence or integrity never makes content authoritative.
A project has one stable objective_id and explicit objective, scope, non-goals, assumptions, evidence standard, and completion standard; objective revisions require itemized acceptance.
Claims, evidence, attempts, reviews, and decisions remain distinct; execution success and integrity checks do not prove a claim.
Every important management write uses base revision, itemized proposals, user decisions, candidate validation, one revision advance, publication, and a receipt.
Every retrieval reports searched and unsearched authorized scope and index freshness; an empty result never proves project-wide absence.
Bind every project operation to one canonical child root, immutable project_id, revision, and compatible entry protocol; fail closed on identity mismatch, ambiguity, or incompatible formal writes.

A managed project has one canonical discoverable SKILL.md. Bootstrap must report when the project is outside the current Codex discovery path, and transaction candidates must never create additional skill entries.

An ordinary conversation has one active project; never switch implicitly, prefer a new conversation after another project's context was loaded, and use explicit read-mostly coordination for intentional cross-project work.
The total skill owns shared behavior and compatibility logic but no concrete project state or mutable authoritative global current-project selection.

governance_invariants.rule: Continuously classify every material work item by layer, data subtype, and audience, then derive authority, storage, validation, version, and release controls; re-evaluate at new branches and lifecycle boundaries and split mixed work before writing.
Framework changes never silently mutate accepted project data, data:project changes never modify framework rules, and developer-only artifacts are never represented as distributed runtime behavior.

A reproducible reusable defect triggers a regression-test proposal; framework test code may use synthetic fixtures, while real cases and gold data remain separately accepted external regression/evaluation data.

A user-raised concern that may involve the framework triggers provisional classification. Already authorized context needs one final preview approval; reading new private or external material first needs one bounded collection approval. There is no automatic upload, and real feedback remains external to project records and framework releases.

capabilities.trigger: The user asks to create or initialize a managed project.
The private machine profile is missing or the user asks to update it.
A confirmed task is being explored or needs to be handed to another conversation.
A .llmpack file must be verified, unpacked, reviewed, or integrated.
Any accepted change is about to be written to project management data.
The user or task searches project knowledge or builds, refreshes, or evaluates an index.
A change is mixed, ambiguous, crosses project/framework authority, or affects runtime and developer audiences differently.
A child project is invoked, an operation resolves a project root, or project identity or compatibility is uncertain.
A legacy, incompatible, or modified child adapter requires inspection or upgrade.
The user explicitly asks to compare or coordinate two or more managed projects.

The user raises a problem that may involve the framework, or a reusable framework defect, compatibility issue, unsafe allowance, blocked valid action, repeated ambiguity, or data-loss/privacy risk is observed.

high.summary: Support merging multiple exploration packages based on the same project revision.

low.summary: Adapt the framework for ChatGPT on the web.
Detect and propose machine-profile changes automatically.
Add package authenticity signatures in addition to integrity hashes.
